title: The reactor's sync protocol has a machine-checked proof of four safety properties, but only for two reactors, one document and five operations
content:
`packages/reactor/specs/tla/ReactorSync.tla` models the sync protocol in TLA+ and TLC checks it. The Phase-1 configuration is deliberately tiny — 2 reactors (`r1`, `r2`), 1 document, 3 operations per reactor, bounded by `nextOpId <= 5` — and explores **357,574 distinct states (1,806,603 generated, max depth 42) in about 11 seconds.**

Four **safety** invariants hold in every state explored:

1. `TypeOK` — all variables well-typed;
2. `OperationUniqueness` — no duplicate operation ids anywhere;
3. `StreamMonotonicity` — operation indices within a stream never decrease;
4. `CursorMonotonicity` — sync cursors never move backwards.

The **liveness** property, `EventualConsistency` (all reactors converge once nothing is in transit), is specified but **not checked** in Phase 1, because the unbounded temporal property is expensive. So "verified" here means safety only.

What the model proves, in the authors' own framing: no data corruption, operation uniqueness within a stream, stream and cursor monotonicity, **idempotency** (an operation received repeatedly creates no duplicate), and that the reshuffle algorithm merges divergent streams deterministically by timestamp.
